subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved with memblock_reserve()

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary: Reviewer Mike Rapoport questioned the necessity of using allocation APIs in the fixed path, citing performance concerns, and suggested that the multi-range CMA path could use allocation APIs but would be slower.
reviews.raw_body:
Fixed path already has the range, why would it use allocation APIs?

The multi-range could, but it will be several times slower and I believe
the intention was to avoid allocation APIs exactly because of that.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to feedback that the patch's use of memblock_reserve() for CMA allocations is an abuse, explaining that it's actually an allocation and not a reservation. The author proposes adding a new helper function to handle this case.
reviews.raw_body:
Having the range doesn't make it a reservation. Both paths take free
memory for the kernel's use, which is an allocation, and an allocation
has to be accepted. memblock_reserve() is for memory that is already in
use: kernel image, initrd, firmware tables. Using it for allocations
leaves acceptance to every caller, and both CMA paths missed it.

If memblock_phys_alloc_range() is the wrong tool, let's add a
memblock_*alloc*() helper that takes the exact range and does the reserve
plus memblock_prep_allocation(), the way memblock_alloc_hugetlb() finishes
its own search. There is no search, so the multi-range path doesn't get
slower, and accept_memory() stays inside memblock.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary:
Reviewer pointed out that memblock_reserve() predates allocation APIs and is used to mark memory as taken, suggesting that the patch should take this into account when accepting memory

Reviewer suggested creating a new helper for reserving and accepting memory, and auditing other callers of memblock_reserve() to ensure consistency.
reviews.raw_body:
memblock_reserve() predates any allocation APIs and it is used to say "I
know this memory is free, I'm taking it". So memory acceptance should have
take it into account.

---

A new helper that does reserve and accept makes sense, but let's do it on
top and also audit other callers of memblock_reserve(). I believe we may
also hit some curious corner cases with memmap=, although this is less
likely.

These two are really simple and easily backportable and I don't see an
issue with calling accept_memory in low level cma code.

cma_declare_contiguous_multi() has other issues and I'm reworking it right
now. But again, that does not mean a simple addition of accept_memory to
CMA contradicts it.

2026-10-29.patch_summary: This patch allows memory reserved by memblock_reserve() to be accepted as Continuous Memory Areas (CMA) for allocation. The change aims to bring consistency in the handling of reserved memory across different kernel APIs, specifically addressing concerns about potential abuse of memblock_reserve().
